The parallel sides of a trapezoid are $ 3$ and $ 9$. The non-parallel sides are $ 4$ and $ 6$. A line parallel to the bases divides the trapezoid into two trapezoids of equal perimeters. The ratio in which each of the non-parallel sides is divided is:

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a trapezoid, with upper base 3, lower base 9, two non-parallel sides respectively 6 and 4, and a line in the middle parallel to the two bases. Let the proportion cut off by this parallel line from the upper base on each leg be x. Since the secant line is parallel to the two bases, the proportions it cuts on the two non-parallel sides are the same, so the upper two leg segments have lengths respectively 6x and 4x. The length of the secant line changes linearly from upper base 3 to lower base 9 according to position, so the length of the secant line is 3+(9-3)x=3+6x. The perimeter of the upper small trapezoid is 3+(3+6x)+6x+4x=6+16x. The perimeter of the lower small trapezoid is 9+(3+6x)+6(1-x)+4(1-x)=22-4x. The two perimeters are equal, so 6+16x=22-4x, solving gives 20x=16, that is x=4/5. Therefore each non-parallel side is divided into upper segment:lower segment as x:(1-x)=4/5:1/5=4:1.

method.method_draft: Let x be the fraction of each non-parallel side cut off in the upper trapezoid, measured from the top base. Because the dividing line is parallel to the bases, it cuts both legs in the same fraction, so the upper leg pieces are 6x and 4x. The length of the new parallel segment changes linearly from 3 to 9, so it is 3+6x. Write the upper perimeter as 3+(3+6x)+6x+4x and the lower perimeter as 9+(3+6x)+6(1-x)+4(1-x). Set these equal and solve for x=4/5, giving top:bottom division ratio x:(1-x)=4:1 on each leg.

method.method_draft: Let the upper pieces of the two non-parallel sides be a and b. The lower pieces are 6-a and 4-b. Since the internal dividing segment belongs to both smaller trapezoids, its length cancels when comparing equal perimeters. Thus equal perimeters give 3+a+b=9+(6-a)+(4-b). Solving gives a+b=8. Because the cut is parallel to the bases, the two legs are divided in the same fraction, so a/6=b/4=t. Then a+b=6t+4t=10t=8, so t=4/5. Therefore each side is divided in the ratio 4/5:1/5=4:1.
method.CoT_raw:
The diagram/context gives a trapezoid with parallel bases 3 and 9 and non-parallel sides 6 and 4. A segment parallel to the bases cuts it into two smaller trapezoids.

Let the upper piece of the side of length 6 be a, and let the upper piece of the side of length 4 be b. Then the lower pieces are 6 - a and 4 - b. The internal parallel segment is part of both smaller trapezoids, so when their perimeters are set equal, that shared segment cancels. Thus the equal-perimeter condition is 3 + a + b = 9 + (6 - a) + (4 - b). Simplifying: 3 + a + b = 19 - a - b, so 2a + 2b = 16, hence a + b = 8.

Because the cutting line is parallel to the bases, it divides both non-parallel sides in the same fraction. Let that upper fraction be t. Then a/6 = b/4 = t, so a = 6t and b = 4t. Therefore a + b = 10t = 8, giving t = 4/5. So each side is divided into an upper part and a lower part in the ratio 4/5 : 1/5 = 4 : 1.
